When you want to express annoyance about present or past situations, you can use modal verbs.
You use the modals might, could, might have and could have to express annoyance.

When you want to talk about past events and you are not sure if they happened or not, you can use modal perfect (modal + past participle).

For example:
You could have forgotten it in the boardroom. (= It's possible that you forgot it in the boardroom. I'm not sure.)
She can't have started the meeting already! (= I don't think she has started the meeting.)
He must have e-mailed you the notes from the meeting. (= I'm almost certain that he e-mailed you.)
They should have started the project by now. (= I think they have started the project.)

images.text:
Denise: They could have offered to reimburse us for that ... Yeah! Well, they shouldn't have changed a thing ... Really? Well, you might have to do something, otherwise, you will have a hornet's nest on your hands ... OK. Let's talk about this later ... [Knocking] Kristi! Come in. Sit down.
Kristi: Business?
Denise: Ugh! There's some trouble with the printers. They may have made a mistake that they could have corrected by now and they had better do something about it. Anyway, how was Winnie's World? I want to hear your perspective.

Kristi: So, first, the good points. I'd like to say that the topic is timely and relevant for children. I think a book like this would be extremely marketable to young people and schools with all the online bullying. Next, the main character is an absolute delight. I could see children relating to this character, but not only that, parents would also feel an affinity toward Winnie. Finally, the writing style has a nice rhythm to it. It reads almost like a song. It has a nice flow.
Denise: Until ... ?
Kristi: Until the ending. I don't like the ending at all. It's too abrupt and just seems to come out of nowhere. The book moves along so nicely until that point. It might seem fine to some people, but for me it almost seems that the author might have been in a rush to finish it. It is definitely missing something that ties the story together. The ending certainly could be better. Honestly, I think it might be a good idea to contact Marisa and discuss setting up a meeting. This might be overstepping my bounds, but I think we should discuss an alternate ending. In any regard, that was my opinion.

Denise: Thank you, Kristi. That was a very thorough review and I completely agree. I enjoyed the book immensely, but that ending could have been better. It left a bad taste in my mouth. Something is missing and I think that ending doesn't fit the narrative.
Kristi: What should we do?
Denise: We'll set up a meeting with Marisa sometime this week.
Kristi: OK. I think that's the best course of action.
